Anton Chekhov, Short Fiction, translated by Constance Garnett.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/anton-chekhov/short-fiction/constance-garnett

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Anton Chekhov, the author, died 1904 (UK for the text used (English translations first published in London 1916-1922 by the British translator); original Russian 1880-1903).
- Constance Garnett, the translator, died 1946.

First publication of the text used: 1922 (SE colophon: 'short stories and novellas published between 1880 and 1903' (original); 'translated from Russian between 1916 and 1922' (translation)).

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1922, before 1931;
  a published work enters the United States public domain 95 years after
  publication, so this work entered it in 2017.
- Country of origin (UK for the text used (English translations first published in London 1916-1922 by the British translator); original Russian 1880-1903): copyright there lasts for life plus 70 years
  after the death of the last surviving person named above. The last to die
  did so in 1946, so the work entered the public domain there on
  1 January 2017.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: stories 1880-1903; Garnett translation 1916-1922; no editor/introducer mentioned
- Wikidata Q2495818 (Constance Garnett, 'English writer and translator 1861-1946'), P570 = 1946-12-17; refs include 'A historical dictionary of British women' and BnF
- English Wikipedia 'Constance Garnett' lead: '19 December 1861 - 17 December 1946'; article cites Oxford DNB 'Garnett, Constance Clara (1861-1946)'. An initial recollection of 1961 was checked and corrected by these sources.
- Wikidata Q89340 (Anton Chekhov), P570 = 1904 (well-established)
